extDescription.message: Redirects domains while keeping path and parameters, and opens a page from a typed ID via a keyboard shortcut.

appTagline.message: Rewrites the domain of a URL while keeping path, query and fragment, and opens a page from a keyboard shortcut.

permBannerText.message: Chrome requires explicit access to both the source and target domains before it can redirect.

redirectsHint.message: The first redirect whose source domain matches is applied. Reorder with the arrows if several rules overlap.

msgIncomplete.message: Fill in both the source and the target domain.

msgMissingPermission.message: Chrome must be allowed to access $1 and $2.

errHostInvalid.message: “$1” is not a valid domain name.

errHostScheme.message: Only http:// and https:// domains are supported.

errSameHost.message: The source and target domains are identical.

testHint.message: Paste a URL you received to check where it will be redirected.

testUnsupportedScheme.message: Only http:// and https:// URLs can be redirected.

testPaused.message: Redirects are paused (switch at the top of the page).

testNoMatch.message: No redirect matches: this URL will open as is.

testMissingPermission.message: (missing permission: the redirect will not apply)

environmentsHint.message: The base URL a search runs against: a production instance, a test environment… The launcher switches between them ([[Alt]]+[[1…9]]).

errBaseUrlEmpty.message: Enter the base URL of the environment.

searchesHint.message: The URL template contains `{q}`, replaced by the value typed in the launcher. Relative to the environment (`/tickets/{q}`) or absolute (`https://support.example.com/t/{q}`). Hash-based URLs work too: `/app#id={q}&model=ticket`. The keyword selects the search from the input field: `t 1234`.

errTemplateNoPlaceholder.message: The template must contain {q}, replaced by the value you type.

shortcutsHint.message: The launcher opens with [[Alt]]+[[Shift]]+[[O]] by default. Chrome lets you pick any combination, and assign a key to the three quick shortcuts below, which open the launcher directly on a given search and environment.

openInNewTab.message: in a new tab (Ctrl+Enter: active tab)

openInCurrentTab.message: in the active tab (Ctrl+Enter: new tab)

backupHint.message: Redirects, environments and searches are synced with your Chrome account. Export lets you share them with a colleague.

importDone.message: Imported: $1 redirect(s), $2 environment(s), $3 search(es). Remember to grant the permissions.

importNothing.message: Nothing to import (duplicates or invalid entries).

popupPausedWouldRedirect.message: Redirects are paused: this URL would be redirected.

popupMissingPermission.message: Missing permission to apply the redirect.

launcherEmptyTitle.message: The launcher is not configured yet.

launcherEmptyNeedEnv.message: Add at least one environment (the base URL) to run a search.

launcherEmptyNeedSearch.message: Add a search (for example “Ticket” → /tickets/{q}) and an environment.

pinnedEnvironmentTitle.message: This search always uses this environment.

launchErrInvalidSearch.message: The URL template of this search is invalid.

launchErrUnsupportedScheme.message: Only http:// and https:// URLs can be opened.

patternHint.message: Use a pattern when the path changes too, not just the domain. `{id}` captures one path segment and is reused in the target; `*` matches part of a segment, `**` anything, and `**` between slashes any number of segments — including none, which covers an optional language prefix. The query string is dropped unless the target adds it back. The fragment (after `#`) is never sent to the server, so a pattern cannot match on it.

errPatternHost.message: The pattern must start with a plain domain name — “$1” is not one.

errPatternDuplicate.message: The placeholder “{$1}” appears twice in the pattern.

errPatternTooMany.message: A pattern can capture at most $1 placeholders.

errPatternNonAscii.message: The pattern must use ASCII characters only.

errTargetInvalid.message: “$1” is not a valid http(s) URL.

errTargetUnknownPlaceholder.message: The target uses “{$1}”, which the pattern does not capture.

errTargetHostPlaceholder.message: The domain of the target URL cannot contain a placeholder.
